aggregate.description:
Group a stored frame by `group_by` and reduce each group's `value` with `aggregation`.

Use it to total or average a frame over one of its dimensions.

`aggregate` skips absent grid cells, not null values. `Frame.build` cannot
represent an in-frame null observation today (`value` must be finite,
`status` is reserved), so "coverage" here means cells present versus
cells expected for the grouped grain. Both figures land in the trace's
`applied_policy` on every call. Unit and facet heterogeneity are checked
before any number is computed. A heterogeneous unit refuses with
candidates to retry against via `unit`, and a heterogeneous facet
refuses naming a differently-scoped `frame_ref` to retry with instead. A
result below the configured coverage floor refuses rather than returning
a number computed from too sparse a grid. Under sum or mean with
`time_period` outside `group_by`, every output row's `time_period` is
one span from the earliest to the latest period the call reduced
(`2018/2022`), the same on every row.

aggregation.description: The reduction function. Closed vocabulary: ['sum', 'mean', 'max', 'min']. Under max or min, each group's digest line carries the period that produced the value in parentheses after it, and if time_period isn't in group_by, the output row's own time_period is that period. When several periods tie for a group's max or min, the earliest of them is reported. Under sum or mean with time_period outside group_by, every output row's time_period is the span the call covers, such as 2018/2022.

group_by.description: Column names to group by before reducing. Empty groups the whole input frame into one row.

place_level.description: Keep only the places at this level before the call, such as Country. Set it when the frame holds places of several levels and the call refuses place_levels_mixed.

rebuild_lost_frames.description: True fetches a frame the analysis service no longer holds again and repeats the call: a spec_ frame at its newest version in the rendering its mint record states, an ops_ frame from its recipe on current data. A spec_ frame with no readable record refuses rendering_not_recorded.

rolling_follows_tree.description: True computes each derived input's rolling years again under this call's one latest year.

anyOf.description:

`currency` is an upper-case ISO 4217 code, `prices` is `current` or
`constant`, and `base_year` is present exactly when prices are constant.
`deflation_basis` names whose prices deflated a constant-price amount and

and a raw materialisation labelled with one span reads as that span.

filter.description:
Keep only the rows of `frame_ref` satisfying every predicate in `predicates`.

Use it to keep the rows of a frame that pass a condition.

Row-value predicates only. An `ordered_threshold` compares a column's
own ordered cell against a threshold, numerically against `value`, or
lexically against `time_period`'s own period string at any grain
(`YYYY`, `YYYY-MM`, `YYYY-MM-DD`). A `category_match` tests a column's
own string cell against a closed set of values. This includes the
`unit` column itself. A `place_level` reads a place's types, such as
a frame's `observationAbout_type` column,
by `common.place_type.levels_of`: a frame that names no place holds
every level of place, and `place_level` on it with `"Country"` keeps
the countries. A `category_match` on `unit` is an ordinary way
to narrow a heterogeneous-unit frame down to one unit, since filter
inspects each row in isolation and never combines two rows' own values
(unlike `aggregate`/`compare`/`growth`/`rank`/`share_of`, filter resolves
no unit or facet before running). An empty result is valid, and the
frame grammar accepts a columns-only empty frame. `frame_ref` may
itself name a prior `aggregate`, `rank` or `growth` result whose
`time_period` is one span such as `2018/2022`. An `ordered_threshold` on
`time_period` refuses over it (`filter_predicate_type_mismatch`, `actual_type` `interval`),
since the span's string says nothing about the periods it covers. A
`category_match` on the exact span string keeps its rows, and a predicate
on any other column filters as usual.

A `time_period` threshold's value may be {anchor: 'latest', offset: n},
which follows the data as growth's window years do.

anchor_key.description: The handle of the stored record of the latest period this call's rolling periods were written from: rak_ and 32 hex digits. Required when the call is rolling and refused when it is not. It is no part of the result's identity.

frame_ref.description: The {spec_id, content_version} pair naming a materialised frame or a prior verb result. Obtained from get_data's or a prior verb's own digest -- never invented. A bare spec_id also works: the server fetches the data itself.

predicates.description: Row-value predicates, applied as a conjunction (a row survives only if it satisfies every predicate). The closed vocabulary: an ordered_threshold (column/op/value, value a number against value or a period string against time_period; refused on time_period when that holds a span such as 2018/2022), a category_match (column/values), or a place_level (column/level), which keeps a row whose place-type column, such as observationAbout_type, names a place at that level, such as Country, to keep one level of place. A role, a window, or a facet binding is out of this grammar: filter narrows by value, and scope is narrowed in get_data's scope argument.

anyOf.description:
`column <op> value` over an ordered column: `value >= 1_000_000`, or
`time_period >= "2015"`, comparing the period string lexically against
`time_period`'s own zero-padded `YYYY`/`YYYY-MM`/`YYYY-MM-DD` forms,
which sort in true chronological order at every grain. A coarser period
compares at its own start, not its own span, so a `"2015"` row satisfies
`gt "2014"` but fails `gte "2015-06"`.

`value` is a number against the numeric `value` column, or a string
against `time_period` or any other column. A string against
`time_period` must be a well-formed period string, checked here ahead
of the engine; a string against any other column passes op-spec
validation unchecked and reaches the engine's own type check instead.
A `RelativeYear` is a `time_period` threshold the runner fills.

rolling.description: Marks a time_period threshold as following the latest period of the data, {anchor: 'latest', offset: 0, rule: 'half1'}, with offset counting whole periods back: value stays the literal period the comparison runs on.

anyOf.description: `column in values`, over a closed, caller-supplied set of category values.

`column`, a place's type enrichment, names a place at `level`.

Reads a `{role}_type` column such as a frame's `observationAbout_type`
column (`Country`,
`AdministrativeArea1,State`), by `common.place_type.levels_of`: a place sits
at each of its types, except that one carrying a Eurostat NUTS type is not
at `Country`. `level="Country"` keeps every country and territory and
leaves out Åland (`nuts/FI2`), whose figures Finland's include.

rebuild_lost_frames.description: True fetches a frame the analysis service no longer holds again and repeats the call: a spec_ frame at its newest version in the rendering its mint record states, an ops_ frame from its recipe on current data. A spec_ frame with no readable record refuses rendering_not_recorded.

rolling.description: The populations the latest period is taken over, {population: [{spec_id, bindings}]}: one entry for each root dataset of the question, bindings narrowing its series as {column: [values]}. growth.description:
Compute each entity's growth across `[window_start, window_end]`.

Use it for the change between two periods, as a percentage or an amount.

`change="relative"` (the default) computes
`growth_rate = (value_end - value_start) / value_start`, the total
percentage change across the window; a zero or sign-crossing base makes
that undefined, so such an entity is excluded as
`zero_or_sign_crossing_base` before any division is attempted.
`change="absolute"` computes `value_end - value_start` directly, in the
input's own unit; that arithmetic is defined over any base. Either mode
excludes an entity whose value overflows as `non_finite`, and the call
refuses (`non_finite_result`) only when every entity is excluded so.

Both modes read only each entity's rows in `window_start` and
`window_end`. Every entity with a row in both is computed, whatever
years between them it lacks; a warning counts the entities with such
gaps. An entity missing either endpoint year is left out and listed
under exclusions as `endpoint_missing`. When no entity has both, the
call refuses (`growth_gap_year`), counting the entities missing each
endpoint and suggesting a window at least one entity holds both ends of,
when one exists.

A window year given as {anchor: 'latest', offset: n} follows the data:
the call takes the newest year at least half of the input's series hold
and moves back -n years. It computes over those literal years, which the
result names, and a card drawn from the result moves forward when new
data lands.

Each output row's `time_period` is the window as a span, such as
`2020/2023`. A frame whose rows already carry a span, such as an
`aggregate` or `rank` result over several years, refuses
(`derived_input_unusable`), because growth reads one row per period.
Retry over the frame that result was computed from.

change.description: 'relative' (the default) computes (value_end - value_start) / value_start; an entity with a zero or sign-crossing base is excluded, since a percentage change is undefined there. 'absolute' computes value_end - value_start directly, keeping the input's own unit; defined over any base, including zero or a sign crossing.

entity_by.description: Column names identifying each entity whose own growth rate is computed. Empty treats the whole frame as one entity's series.

rolling.description: Marks window_start, window_end, or both as following the latest period of the data: {window_end: {anchor: 'latest', offset: 0, rule: 'half1'}}, with offset counting whole years back from the latest. rank.description:
Rank entities identified by `rank_by`, optionally reducing each
entity's own rows with `aggregation` first.

Use it to order entities by a value, such as the largest donors in a
year, and to keep the top or bottom few.

Ranks what's present. An entity absent from the window simply isn't
ranked. Competition ranking ("1224"). Entities sharing a value share a
rank number, and the rank number never breaks a tie. The *order* two
tied entities are listed in is broken deterministically by the frame
grammar's own total ordering over `rank_by`'s values. Refuses
(`coverage_insufficient`, reusing `aggregate`'s own floor) when the
grid, every ranked entity times every distinct period any entity
contributes as reflected in the input data rather than the window's
full calendar range, falls below the configured coverage floor. A
period where no entity has any data at all is invisible to this check.

A window year given as {anchor: 'latest', offset: n} follows the data
as growth's window years do.

Collapsed, every output row's `time_period` is the extent of the
periods the window holds, such as `2018/2022`, or that one period when
the window holds only one. A frame whose rows carry one span, such as
a growth result, keeps that span; a window keeps a span row only when
it covers every year of the span.

`per_period=True` ranks each of the window's periods on its own instead
of collapsing them: with no `limit`, the output frame's own `value`
column carries each entity's rank *position* per period, not its
measured value, and no
verb here may read that position as a quantity to ratio (`share_of`) or
grow at a percentage rate (`growth` with `change="relative"`) or rank
again -- all three refuse (`derived_input_ordinal`) over this call's own
output, or over anything derived from it. A top or bottom N per period
is this call with `limit` set.

`limit` keeps the entities ranked at that position or better in the
output frame, every one tied at the boundary included, with their
measured values in either mode: a limited per-period rank writes no
ordinal marker. Coverage and the floor check cover every ranked entity,
and the rows left out are reported as a `beyond_limit` exclusion.

resolve_anchor.description:
Find the latest period of the data a question's rolling periods follow.

The latest period is the newest calendar year at least half of the series
of every population hold. A series is one combination of a frame's columns
other than `time_period`, `value` and `status`.

Use it before a rolling `growth`, `rank` or `filter` call, to find the
latest period the data holds.

The result is stored, and its `anchor_key` goes on every rolling `growth`,
`rank` and `filter` call of the question, whose literal periods are
`period` moved back by each rolling offset. This tool computes no frame
and returns no {spec_id, content_version} pair.

populations.description: The populations the latest period is taken over: one {spec_id, bindings} for each root dataset of the question, bindings narrowing its series as {column: [values]}, and levels, when set, holding a place-type column to one level of place as {column: level}. A keyed share_of or join whose two sides both count is one {pair: [left populations, right populations], keys: {left column: right column}} instead. share_of.description:
Divide a numerator by a denominator, per matched (key, period).

`operation` picks the form. `share` (the default) gives the numerator's
share of its whole in per cent, unit `Percent` (5.3 means 5.3%), the unit
a published "% of GDP" series carries. `quotient` divides one measure by
another in different units, such as GDP by population; the result's unit
is "<numerator's unit> per <denominator's unit>", and a side that is a
share, a growth rate or a quotient already refuses
(`quotient_of_side_unit_unsupported`). Either way the result is one series
under its own stat_var.

Each side is narrowed by its own `entity` binding, then every remaining
row sharing both `numerator_by`'s key values and a `time_period` is
summed. `numerator_by` left empty (the default) gives one row per period,
no role columns. `denominator_by` pairs each `numerator_by` column with
the denominator's column carrying that role, by name; left empty, the
denominator is pooled (one total per period, shared by every numerator
key). A non-empty `denominator_by` must name every `numerator_by`
column, and a share refuses a key outside `numerator_by`
(`op_spec_invalid`). A numerator key with no denominator match, a key
sharing no period, and a period one side holds alone are left out and
recorded, never counted as zero; the digest names them. The call refuses
only when nothing is left to divide (`share_of_key_unmatched`,
`share_of_grain_mismatch`, `quotient_of_no_key_matched`,
`comparison_periods_disjoint`). A period whose denominator sums to zero
refuses a share (`share_of_zero_denominator`, retryable with another
denominator source); a quotient leaves that cell out and refuses only
when every cell divides by zero (`quotient_of_zero_denominator`). A
genuine overflow (`non_finite_result`) is not retryable.

denominator_by.description: {numerator_by column: denominator column carrying that same role}, pairing the two sides by name, never by position. Every numerator_by column must be a key here (a partial mapping refuses). Omit (the default) for a pooled denominator: one total per period, shared by every numerator key.

denominator_entity.description: Same as numerator_entity, for the denominator side.

denominator_frame_ref.description: The denominator's frame_ref. Omit to compute a share within two slices of the same frame_ref, narrowed by numerator_entity/denominator_entity instead.

denominator_unit.description: Pins the denominator's unit: one of a unit_heterogeneous refusal's fix.units values, a unit ref, a converted unit's {currency, prices, base_year, deflation_basis} object, or a composed unit's {numerator, denominator} object.

frame_ref.description: The numerator's {spec_id, content_version} pair, naming a materialised frame or a prior verb result. Obtained from get_data's or a prior verb's own digest -- never invented. A bare spec_id also works: the server fetches the data itself.

numerator_by.description: Role column(s), on the numerator's own frame, to key the output by -- one row per (key, period) instead of one row per period. These become the output frame's own role columns. Empty (the default) computes a single figure, with no role columns.

numerator_entity.description: {role_column: value} narrowing the numerator's own rows before summing each period. Empty sums every row on this side per period except group totals, residuals included; a whole total (party_whole true) of a class no member holds stays, and one that may hold a member refuses. A filter to member_kinds is for comparing or ranking members; before a sum it leaves out the residuals. For a total across a whole side, search naming the population ("all donors") with no operation over that side. Role columns only -- stat_var and time_period are not accepted selectors.

anyOf.description:
A converted unit, as `get_data` writes it into a frame's `unit` cells:
`currency` is an upper-case ISO 4217 code, `prices` is `current` or
`constant`, and `base_year` is present exactly when prices are constant.
`deflation_basis` names whose prices deflated a constant-price amount and
is valid only at constant prices.
A composed unit's object, as a unit_heterogeneous refusal lists it.

numerator_unit.description: Pins the numerator's unit: one of a unit_heterogeneous refusal's fix.units values, a unit ref, a converted unit's {currency, prices, base_year, deflation_basis} object, or a composed unit's {numerator, denominator} object.

operation.description: share (the default): the numerator as a per cent of its whole, in one unit. quotient: one measure per unit of another in two different units, such as GDP per person.

place_level.description: Keep only the places at this level before the call, such as Country. Set it when the frame holds places of several levels and the call refuses place_levels_mixed. The denominator is filtered too, so a denominator bound to a group entity such as the world is left out.
